entries.title: Context multiplier
entries.tip: Your 10th message can cost 11x more than your first because Claude rereads the full conversation each turn.

entries.title: Output also counts
entries.tip: Every word Claude generates is billed too. Shorter answers save both input and output tokens.

entries.title: Edit, don't follow up
entries.tip: Instead of sending a correction message when Claude makes a mistake, click 'edit' on your original prompt and fix the wording. This replaces the exchange in the history rather than adding to it.

entries.title: Batch your questions
entries.tip: Combine multiple tasks into a single message. One prompt with three tasks equals one context load, whereas three separate messages result in three context loads.

entries.title: Fresh chat every 15–20
entries.tip: Start a new conversation every 15 to 20 messages. Ask Claude to summarize the current chat first, then paste that summary as the starting point of the new chat to ditch the bloat.

entries.title: Use fewer tokens
entries.tip: Shift your mindset from counting messages to counting tokens. Since Claude rereads the entire history every turn, the 10th message costs significantly more than the first.

entries.title: Track token usage
entries.tip: Install a local dashboard or check your machine's JSONL log files to see real input/output token data. You can't fix what you can't measure.

entries.title: Upload to projects
entries.tip: Upload recurring files (PDFs, style guides, contracts) to the 'Projects' feature once. This allows Claude to reference them without retokenizing the document every time.

entries.title: Set up memory
entries.tip: Use 'Memory and User Settings' to save your role and communication style permanently. This stops you from burning tokens on 'Act as a...' setup prompts in every chat.

entries.title: Turn off unused features
entries.tip: Disable web search, connectors, and 'Advanced Thinking' if you don't need them. These features add tokens to every response.

entries.title: Use Haiku for simple tasks
entries.tip: Use the Haiku model for brainstorming, formatting, or grammar checks. It handles these tasks at a much lower cost than Sonnet or Opus.

entries.title: Enable overage safety net
entries.tip: Enable the overage feature in usage settings. This switches to pay-as-you-go billing at API rates when limits are hit, so you don't lose work.

entries.title: Spread work sessions
entries.tip: Claude uses a rolling 5-hour window. Divide your work into morning, afternoon, and evening sessions to let your usage reset throughout the day.

entries.title: Work during off-peak
entries.tip: Perform resource-intensive tasks in the evening or on weekends. Usage limits may be consumed more quickly during peak hours (5 AM–11 AM PT).

entries.title: Early morning ping
entries.tip: Send a tiny message early in the morning (e.g., 6 AM) to start your rolling 5-hour window before you actually sit down to work.

entries.title: Talk like a caveman
entries.tip: Instruct Claude to drop the fluff and talk like a caveman. This can reduce output token consumption by up to 65%.

entries.title: Anchor on concrete outputs
entries.tip: Tell Claude exactly what file, function, or artifact it should produce — vague goals cause wandering.

entries.title: Break long pipelines
entries.tip: Split multi-step agent tasks into discrete checkpoints. Verify each step before moving to the next.

entries.title: Define abort conditions
entries.tip: Tell Claude when to stop and report back rather than keep trying — e.g. 'if you can't find it in 3 attempts, halt'.

entries.title: Dry-run first
entries.tip: Ask Claude to describe the actions it intends to take before it takes them. Catch mistakes before they run.

entries.title: Gate destructive actions
entries.tip: Instruct Claude to ask before deleting files, sending messages, or making API writes.

entries.title: Parallelize sub-tasks
entries.tip: For independent sub-tasks (e.g. research + code + docs), launch them as separate chats and merge results.

entries.title: State your success criteria
entries.tip: Include a measurable outcome in your prompt — 'done when all tests pass' beats 'make it work'.

entries.title: Use structured output
entries.tip: Ask for JSON or XML when the result feeds another process. Structured output is easier to parse and validate.

entries.title: Keep claude.md lean
entries.tip: Keep your claude.md project file lean (under 200 lines) and use it as an index.
entries.source: Stop Wasting Your Claude Tokens. Do This Instead... by Rick Mulready

entries.title: Limit unused MCP servers
entries.tip: Limit MCP servers and Claude skills to only those used in at least 20% of sessions.
entries.source: Stop Wasting Your Claude Tokens. Do This Instead... by Rick Mulready

entries.title: Manually compact chat
entries.tip: Manually compact the chat when usage reaches 50–60%.
entries.source: Stop Wasting Your Claude Tokens. Do This Instead... by Rick Mulready

entries.title: Monitor token usage
entries.tip: Use '/context' and 'status line' commands in Claude Code to monitor token usage.
entries.source: Stop Wasting Your Claude Tokens. Do This Instead... by Rick Mulready

entries.title: Respect the cache rule
entries.tip: Mind the 'Five-Minute Cache Rule' — reprocess after inactivity to avoid spikes.
entries.source: Stop Wasting Your Claude Tokens. Do This Instead... by Rick Mulready

entries.title: Save preferences
entries.tip: Save your role, style, and formatting once in memory instead of retyping it every new chat.

entries.title: Save progress before compacting
entries.tip: Save progress and update progress/plan files before compacting or taking a break.
entries.source: Stop Wasting Your Claude Tokens. Do This Instead... by Rick Mulready

entries.title: Upload recurring files
entries.tip: Put repeated documents in Projects once. Cached content avoids repeated retokenization.

entries.title: Always include a test case
entries.tip: Provide sample input and expected output in your prompt. Claude writes tighter code when it can self-check.

entries.title: Ask for comments sparingly
entries.tip: Request inline comments only for non-obvious logic. Excessive comments inflate output tokens with little value.

entries.title: Constrain the interface
entries.tip: Specify the exact function signature, class structure, or API contract before asking Claude to implement it.

entries.title: Diff before accepting
entries.tip: For edits to existing code, ask Claude to show a diff view. Review changes before pasting in.

entries.title: Name the language explicitly
entries.tip: Say 'Python 3.11' not just 'Python' — version hints prevent deprecated patterns.

entries.title: Pass failing tests as context
entries.tip: Paste the test that's failing alongside the code. Claude fixes the right thing when it sees both.

entries.title: Pin your dependencies
entries.tip: Include the library name and version when asking for integration code. Avoids outdated API calls.

entries.title: Request minimal diffs
entries.tip: Ask Claude to change only what's necessary. 'Keep the rest of the file intact' prevents over-editing.

entries.title: Show the error message
entries.tip: Copy the exact error text into your prompt. Stack traces and error codes beat vague descriptions.

entries.title: Specify the output format
entries.tip: For scripts, say 'print to stdout', 'return a dict', or 'write to file'. Ambiguity wastes iterations.

entries.title: Use Plan Mode
entries.tip: Use Plan Mode to avoid wasted tokens on incorrect directions.
entries.source: Stop Wasting Your Claude Tokens. Do This Instead... by Rick Mulready

entries.title: Bisect the problem
entries.tip: Ask Claude to identify which half of the code contains the bug before attempting a fix.

entries.title: Check assumptions first
entries.tip: Before diving into a fix, ask Claude to list its assumptions. Wrong assumptions cause wrong fixes.

entries.title: Give full stack traces
entries.tip: Paste the complete traceback, not just the last line. Context lines often contain the real cause.

entries.title: Isolate the repro case
entries.tip: Ask Claude to produce the smallest code snippet that reproduces the issue before adding a fix.

entries.title: Name the environment
entries.tip: OS, runtime version, and framework matter. 'Python 3.11 on macOS ARM' beats 'my machine'.

entries.title: Provide before/after
entries.tip: Show what used to work and what changed. Regression bugs are much faster to fix with a changelog.

entries.title: Request root cause first
entries.tip: Ask 'What is causing this?' before 'Fix it'. Understanding the cause often reveals a better solution.

entries.title: Ask for trade-offs
entries.tip: Request pros/cons or multiple approaches before committing. Prevents lock-in to a suboptimal path.

entries.title: Define constraints up front
entries.tip: State performance targets, size limits, and compatibility requirements before asking for a design.

entries.title: Generate an ADR
entries.tip: Ask Claude to produce an Architecture Decision Record for major choices. Great for team knowledge transfer.

entries.title: Map dependencies first
entries.tip: Before writing code, ask Claude to map all dependencies and interactions. Catches integration issues early.

entries.title: Plan in plain language
entries.tip: Get a written plan approved before any code is generated. Cheap to change text, expensive to change code.

entries.title: Request a checklist
entries.tip: For complex tasks, ask Claude to generate a checklist first. Use it to track completion without re-explaining context.

entries.title: Separate design from implementation
entries.tip: Ask for schema or interface design in one message, implementation in the next. Each step stays focused.

entries.title: Work top-down
entries.tip: Start with system design, then modules, then functions. Claude produces more coherent code with the big picture.

entries.title: Add a persona
entries.tip: Assigning a role ('you are a senior security engineer') focuses Claude's vocabulary and priorities.

entries.title: Assign explicit constraints
entries.tip: Hard constraints beat soft ones. 'Do not use external libraries' is clearer than 'try to minimize dependencies'.

entries.title: Chain-of-thought for hard problems
entries.tip: Add 'think step by step' for math, logic, or planning tasks. Dramatically reduces errors on multi-step reasoning.

entries.title: Few-shot examples work
entries.tip: Provide 2–3 input/output examples in your prompt for format-sensitive tasks. Better than describing the format in words.

entries.title: Give negative examples too
entries.tip: Show Claude what you don't want alongside what you do. Reduces the chance of drifting toward common but wrong patterns.

entries.title: Ground with real data
entries.tip: Paste in real filenames, real error messages, real schema names. Specificity dramatically improves quality.

entries.title: Separate context from instruction
entries.tip: Use clear delimiters (e.g. <doc>...</doc>) to separate background context from the actual task.

entries.title: Specify the audience
entries.tip: 'Explain to a junior developer' vs. 'explain to a principal engineer' yields very different, more useful answers.

entries.title: Temperature via words
entries.tip: Say 'be creative and explore unusual options' or 'be conservative and follow best practices' instead of adjusting sliders.

entries.title: Use XML for structure
entries.tip: Wrapping context in XML tags (<instructions>, <context>, <examples>) produces more reliable parsing by Claude.

entries.title: Ask for citations
entries.tip: For research tasks, ask Claude to include citations or note when it's uncertain. Reduces hallucination risk.

entries.title: Draft then refine
entries.tip: Get a rough draft first, then ask for targeted rewrites. Cheaper than generating polished prose in one shot.

entries.title: Give a word count
entries.tip: Specify 'about 200 words' or 'at least 400 words'. Vague length requests produce wildly inconsistent output.

entries.title: Request an outline first
entries.tip: For long documents, get an outline approved before generating full content. Prevents wasted prose.

entries.title: Set the reading level
entries.tip: 'Write at a 5th grade reading level' or 'assume PhD-level reader' tunes vocabulary and sentence complexity.

entries.title: Specify tone explicitly
entries.tip: 'Formal', 'conversational', 'technical', 'enthusiastic' — tone words do more work than vague quality adjectives.

entries.title: Summarize long docs first
entries.tip: Paste a long document and ask for a summary before asking specific questions. Orients Claude to the material.

entries.title: Audit Claude's code
entries.tip: Treat Claude-generated code as a junior dev's PR — review for security issues before merging to production.

entries.title: Never paste credentials
entries.tip: Scrub API keys, tokens, and passwords from any code before pasting into a chat prompt.

entries.title: Redact PII
entries.tip: Replace real names, emails, and personal data with placeholders before sharing logs or data files.

entries.title: Sanitize before paste
entries.tip: Strip internal URLs, hostnames, and internal identifiers from prompts shared in logged sessions.

entries.title: Test in sandbox first
entries.tip: Run Claude-generated scripts in a sandbox or staging environment before touching production.

entries.title: Validate external sources
entries.tip: If Claude fetches or references external data, verify URLs and sources before trusting the output.

entries.title: Ask Claude to break its own code
entries.tip: After generating a function, ask Claude to list edge cases and failure modes it didn't handle.

entries.title: Generate test cases separately
entries.tip: Ask for tests in a separate prompt from the implementation. Mixed prompts produce incomplete coverage.

entries.title: Mutation testing prompts
entries.tip: Ask Claude to deliberately introduce bugs, then fix them. Confirms your tests actually catch issues.

entries.title: Request property-based tests
entries.tip: For data-heavy logic, ask for property-based tests (e.g. Hypothesis/fast-check). Finds edge cases automatically.

entries.title: Review assertions explicitly
entries.tip: Ask Claude to explain why each assertion is correct. Surfaces wrong tests that pass for the wrong reason.

entries.title: Test error paths
entries.tip: Ask specifically for tests that cover failure modes — not just the happy path.

entries.title: Chain outputs as inputs
entries.tip: Pass Claude's JSON output directly into the next prompt as structured input. Reduces re-typing and parsing errors.

entries.title: Create reusable templates
entries.tip: For recurring tasks (PR descriptions, changelogs, release notes), build fill-in-the-blank prompt templates.

entries.title: Integrate with your editor
entries.tip: Use Claude Code CLI or a VS Code extension so you can invoke Claude without switching windows.

entries.title: Pipe CLI output directly
entries.tip: Redirect terminal output (logs, test results) directly into a Claude prompt with heredoc or piping.

entries.title: Use Projects for team context
entries.tip: Store shared system prompts, style guides, and codebase docs in a Project so the whole team stays aligned.

entries.title: Wire into CI
entries.tip: Use Claude API in CI to auto-generate PR summaries, flag risky diffs, or suggest test names for new functions.
